manifest.name: html-style: embedded pages, and where theme colours compile

context.rationale: Your walkthrough notes on steps 14 and 15 asked for these two passages committed and offered for approval: "embedded page" in place of "tenant page" with the same examples, and a much tighter convention 7 with no dated reference. Rule 5 also takes two facts the Budget DRS appendix fixes established: a list over a strip needs an h-dvh root, and width queries inside a frame measure the frame. Approve, approve with edits, or return it.

items.commentary: Rule 5 is retitled for an embedded page and keeps its three examples. It adds two things: rule 12's list over a strip takes an h-dvh root, which document scrolling alone had ruled out, and width queries measure the frame, not the window. @@ -210,7 +210,7 @@ composition views. Demo:
 4. Alpine's `x-data`, `x-show`, `x-bind` for reactivity: no React
 5. Use Phosphor Icons via CDN for iconography: no inline SVGs. A project's or repository's own mark is the exception: an SVG file drawn to the [Drawn marks](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/docs/favicons/README.md#drawn-marks) rules.
 6. No `<style>` blocks: no vanilla CSS, no `<style type="text/tailwindcss">`, no `@apply`. Generally, avoid all efforts to override styles in third-party components. Where no utility can reach, write `/* exempt(<kind>): <reason> */` before the rule, with a kind from [`python/css-blocks.py`](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/python/css-blocks.py). Enforced by `npm run css-scan`, gated in `node/test/css-blocks.test.mjs` against [`docs/css-baseline.csv`](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/docs/css-baseline.csv), a per-file ceiling; after converting a file, lower its row with `--write`.
-7. A daisyUI semantic colour works only in the utility families daisyUI itself ships, and there are **exactly three**: `bg`, `border`, `text`. Derived from daisyUI 5.7.28's own stylesheet on 2026-09-08, not estimated: it defines 207 classes on a semantic colour across 25 families, and every family but those three is a daisyUI COMPONENT (`btn-primary`, `badge-error`, `alert-warning`), which is a different thing. So `bg-base-200`, `text-base-content` and `border-base-300` resolve, while `divide-base-200`, `ring-primary`, `outline-primary`, `accent-primary`, `from-base-100`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-`, `stroke-`, `caret-`, `placeholder-`, `decoration-` and `shadow-` on a semantic colour all compile to nothing and are dropped silently. **The fix is mechanical: write the same utility with an arbitrary value, `ring-primary` to `ring-[var(--color-primary)]`.** Measured 2026-09-08 in headless Chromium: the arbitrary form sets `--tw-ring-color` to the theme colour where the semantic name set nothing, `divide-[var(--color-base-200)]` paints at `oklch(0.98 0 0)` where `divide-base-200` painted in the text colour, and an opacity step rides along unchanged (`/40` becomes `color-mix(... 40%, transparent)`). So the ring stays a ring and takes no layout space, which swapping to `border-*` would not preserve, and the colour still follows the theme, which a palette colour would not. One exception measured: `shadow-*` leaves `--tw-shadow-color` unset in the arbitrary form, so a shadow tint has to be written out. **Run it rather than remember it: `npm run family-scan`** ([`python/dead-family.py`](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/python/dead-family.py)), which derives the supported set from the installed daisyUI, names the substitution per finding, and gates the tree in `node/test/dead-family.test.mjs`. Tailwind v4 then defaults `border-color` to `currentColor` (v3 defaulted to `gray-200`), so `divide-y` alone paints hairlines in the **text colour**: black lines where a faint grey was intended. The same trap waits in `ring-*`, `outline-*`, and `accent-*`. Separate rows with `gap`, or write the border explicitly (`[&>*+*]:border-t [&>*+*]:border-base-200`). A Tailwind palette name (`divide-slate-300`) also works and is the tell: if swapping the colour name fixes it, the semantic name was never compiling. Inside an `x-for`, reach for the index rather than the adjacency selector; see 8.
+7. **A daisyUI theme colour compiles in three utility families, `bg`, `border` and `text`, unless the page registers the theme colours with Tailwind.** On a page without the registration, `divide-base-200`, `ring-primary`, `outline-`, `from-`, `fill-`, `stroke-` and the rest compile to nothing and drop silently, while components such as `btn-primary` work. `lib/gh-boot.js` registers them on every page that boots the web-tools loader, and a page can register them itself with an `@theme inline` block. Elsewhere, write the same utility with an arbitrary value, `ring-[var(--color-primary)]`, which keeps the theme colour and any opacity step; a `shadow-*` tint has no arbitrary form, so drop the tint or write out the whole shadow. `npm run family-scan` ([`python/dead-family.py`](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/python/dead-family.py)) finds such utilities and names the fix, and [its tests](https://github.com/mehrlander/web-tools/blob/main/node/test/dead-family.test.mjs) hold the measured cases. Tailwind v4 also defaults the border colour to `currentColor`, so `divide-y` alone draws text-coloured hairlines: separate rows with `gap`, or colour the border (`[&>*+*]:border-t [&>*+*]:border-base-200`; inside an `x-for`, see 8).
 8. **Structural selectors are wrong inside an `x-for`, including the adjacency fix above.** Alpine inserts each clone *after* the `<template>` rather than replacing it, so the template stays in the DOM and occupies the parent's first child slot. items.commentary: Convention 7 now says the three-family limit holds only on a page that does not register the theme colours, and lib/gh-boot.js registers them on every page that boots the web-tools loader. It is cut from about 2,400 characters to about 1,200; the dated measurements give way to a link to the scan's tests, which hold the measured cases. The shadow exception now says what to do instead, and the currentColor hairline trap and the border fix that convention 8 points back to are kept.
